beginner.summary: For Python developers who have called an LLM API and want to build stateful agents with LangGraph. Covers installing langgraph, StateGraph with TypedDict and Pydantic state, nodes and edges, reducers and add_messages, conditional routing, ToolNode and the tool-calling loop, compiling and visualizing graphs, checkpointers and thread IDs, state inspection, streaming modes, input and output schemas, retries and recursion limits, interrupt and Command(resume), create_agent, message trimming, testing with fake models, LangSmith tracing, and a support triage capstone.
prerequisites: Writes Python 3.10 or later with functions, classes, type hints and virtual environments
Has called a chat model API such as OpenAI, Anthropic or a local Ollama model and knows what a tool call is
Has a laptop with Python, pip or uv, an editor such as Visual Studio Code and an API key or a local model for the labs
outcomes: Build, compile, invoke and visualize a StateGraph with typed state, reducers and conditional edges
Run a tool-calling agent loop with ToolNode and persist conversations by thread_id with a checkpointer
Pause a graph for human approval with interrupt and resume it with Command
Test a graph without a live model and trace its runs in LangSmith

intermediate.summary: For developers who have shipped a basic LangGraph agent and now need parallelism, reusable subgraphs, durable persistence and multi-agent designs. Covers fan-out and fan-in, the Send API, Command, subgraphs, custom stream events, SQLite and Postgres checkpointers, time travel, richer interrupt patterns, long-term memory with stores and semantic search, caching and retries, the functional API, supervisor and swarm agents, agentic RAG, tool injection, context engineering, langgraph dev with Studio, LangSmith evaluation, and a research assistant capstone.
prerequisites: Has built a StateGraph with reducers, conditional edges, ToolNode and a checkpointer
Can read a LangSmith trace and write pytest tests with fake chat models
Has Docker or a local PostgreSQL instance available and an API key or local model for the labs
outcomes: Run work in parallel with fan-out, Send map-reduce and deferred nodes and merge results with reducers
Compose subgraphs and multi-agent supervisor or swarm systems that stream events and persist in SQLite or Postgres
Add long-term memory with a store, time travel and richer human review patterns
Serve a graph locally with langgraph dev and evaluate it with LangSmith datasets

advanced.summary: For engineers who run LangGraph agents in production or lead the design of agent platforms. Covers the Pregel execution model, custom channels and state migration, durable execution and idempotency, Postgres checkpointer operations and retention, hierarchical teams, dynamic graphs, escalation workflows, background runs, crons and double-texting, streaming at scale, container builds, Kubernetes hosting, custom auth, guardrails, cost control, observability, regression gating with evaluation, MCP and A2A interoperability, JavaScript parity, and a platform capstone.
prerequisites: Has built graphs with subgraphs, Send, interrupts, a Postgres checkpointer and a store
Operates services with Docker, PostgreSQL and basic Kubernetes objects such as Deployment, Service and Secret
Has LangSmith experiments or comparable evaluation experience and an existing agent to harden
outcomes: Explain and exploit the Pregel superstep model, channels and durability modes to design correct, restartable agents
Deploy and operate LangGraph Server with Postgres, Redis, authentication, background runs and tuned streaming
Control risk, cost and quality with guardrails, token budgets, tracing, alerts and evaluation gates in CI
Lead a design review for a multi-agent platform including interoperability and a TypeScript counterpart
